conventions: Every new .ts/.tsx file starts with the Apache-2.0 block header exactly as in plugins/notifications/src/plugin.ts, with the line 'Copyright 2026 The Backstage Authors'. Never change the year on an existing file.

Formatting is Prettier with the repo config (@backstage/cli/config/prettier): 2-space indent, single quotes, trailing commas, semicolons, 80-column wrap, arrow functions with a single parameter written without parentheses (x => x).

Named exports only (ADR003); the only default export stays the existing createFrontendPlugin export in plugins/notifications/src/alpha.tsx. Function components take a typed props parameter; never React.FC (ADR006). No default React import: import hooks and types by name from 'react'.
Per-module imports for utility libraries, as the package already does: import throttle from 'lodash/throttle'; import useAsyncRetry from 'react-use/esm/useAsyncRetry'.

UI in plugins/notifications uses @backstage/ui (Flex, Text, ButtonIcon), @backstage/core-components (Link, Progress, ResponseErrorPanel) and @remixicon/react icons; styling goes in the component's existing CSS module, never inline style objects.

Every user-visible string in plugins/notifications comes from notificationsTranslationRef through const { t } = useTranslationRef(notificationsTranslationRef), with useTranslationRef imported from '@backstage/core-plugin-api/alpha' and the ref from the relative 'translation' module.

Every symbol newly exported from a package entry point (src/index.ts, src/alpha.tsx) has a TSDoc comment with a release tag (@public, or @alpha in alpha.tsx). report*.api.md files are only written by the API report tooling, never typed.

Tests run on Jest through backstage-cli (CI=1 yarn test <path>). In plugins/notifications use React Testing Library (screen, findBy*, fireEvent from '@testing-library/react'), renderInTestApp and TestApiProvider from '@backstage/test-utils', and jest-dom matchers (already loaded by src/setupTests.ts). Prefer findBy* and waitForElementToBeRemoved over waitFor. Add no test IDs to implementation code. Prefer a few thorough tests with several assertions each.

Mock APIs in tests are plain objects of jest.fn() cast to the API type (for example { getNotifications: jest.fn(), ... } as unknown as NotificationsApi), passed through TestApiProvider apis={[[notificationsApiRef, api], [toastApiRef, toastApi]]}; toastApiRef comes from '@backstage/frontend-plugin-api' and signalApiRef from '@backstage/plugin-signals-react'.

Notification fixtures in tests are full Notification objects from '@backstage/plugin-notifications-common': { id, user: 'user:default/guest', created: new Date(...), origin: 'test', payload: { title, severity: 'normal' } }.

Documentation follows docs/contribute/doc-style-guide.md: U.S. English, second person, present tense, sentence-case headings, code style for package names, paths and props, fenced code blocks tagged with a language (tsx, yaml).

Changesets are hand-written markdown files in .changeset/ with front matter of the form '<package name in single quotes>': patch, then one short paragraph for adopters that names no internal function, class or variable.

decisions.choice: The old-system card extension is the public export UnreadNotificationsCard (plugins/notifications/src/plugin.ts, re-exported from src/index.ts); its props type UnreadNotificationsCardProps = { limit?: number; pollingIntervalMs?: number } is public; the rendered component UnreadNotificationsCardContent stays internal to the package (exported from its folder only, not from src/index.ts or src/components/index.ts).
rejected: exporting the content component from the package entry
decisions.reason: Matches the folder name the brief names, and keeps the public API to the extension and its props, like the other home cards.

decisions.choice: limit defaults to 5 and pollingIntervalMs to 60000, both through prop destructuring defaults in UnreadNotificationsCardContent; no exported constants.
decisions.reason: Defaults approved at Gate 1; both overridable through props.

decisions.choice: Inside UnreadNotificationsCardContent, no new hook file: a refresh boolean state, a lodash throttle(setRefresh, 2000) for signals (leading edge, same as NotificationsPage), an effect that calls retry() and resets refresh when refresh is true and loading is false, a setInterval effect only when isSignalsAvailable is false, and an unmount cleanup that cancels the throttle.
rejected: a new useUnreadNotifications hook in src/hooks
decisions.reason: Single consumer; the throttle-plus-refresh-flag pattern is the one NotificationsPage already uses, and it gives at most one request per signal burst or tick (NFR-4).

decisions.choice: The card keeps the shown items in local state, replaced from each fetch result; a successful updateNotifications({ ids: [id], read: true }) filters that id out of local state without refetching; a failure leaves the item and posts toastApi.post({ title: t('unreadNotificationsCard.errors.markAsReadFailed'), status: 'danger' }).
rejected: an inline error message in the card
decisions.reason: Removal is immediate; the next signal or poll fills the list. The toast mirrors how NotificationsTable reports failed bulk actions.

decisions.choice: The card resolves the page root with useRouteRef(rootRouteRef)() inside a try block (the hook throws after its own hooks when the route is not mounted) and falls back to '/notifications'; item links are `${root}?id=${encodeURIComponent(notification.id)}`, the View all link is the root.
decisions.reason: FR-3: use the plugin route, still render in tests and apps without the page; the hook count is the same on every render.

decisions.topic: Deep link on the notifications page
decisions.choice: NotificationsPage reads id with useSearchParams from 'react-router-dom'. When the current page result is loaded and does not contain that id, it fetches getNotification(id) (a rejection resolves to undefined) and passes [pinned, ...pageNotifications] to the table; the table gets highlightedNotificationId and marks the matching row's content Flex with aria-current="true" and the CSS module class highlighted.
rejected: fetching by id even when the item is already on the page
aria-selected on the table row (material-table does not expose row attributes)
decisions.reason: Placement approved at Gate 1 (pin at the top, keep filters). The table keeps its page size, so while a pinned row is shown it is the first of pageSize visible rows; clearing ?id restores the plain page.

units.behaviour: Home card content listing the signed-in user's latest unread notifications with deep links, mark-as-read, empty, error and loading states, refreshed by signals or by polling.
rules: 1. Destructure props with defaults limit = 5 and pollingIntervalMs = 60000; UnreadNotificationsCardProps carries a TSDoc comment with @public and a TSDoc line on each field (limit: maximum number of notifications shown, default 5; pollingIntervalMs: refresh interval used only when signals are unavailable, default 60000).

2. Hooks, all called unconditionally and in this order: useTranslationRef(notificationsTranslationRef); useApi(notificationsApiRef); useApi(toastApiRef) with toastApiRef from '@backstage/frontend-plugin-api'; the route root per the 'Deep-link href and route fallback' decision; useSignal<NotificationSignal>('notifications') giving lastSignal and isSignalsAvailable; useNotificationsApi from '../../hooks' calling api.getNotifications({ read: false, limit, sort: 'created', sortOrder: 'desc' }) with deps [limit].
3. Local state items: Notification[] | undefined, set to value.notifications by an effect on [value] whenever value is defined.

4. Refresh: const [refresh, setRefresh] = useState(false); throttledSetRefresh = useMemo(() => throttle(setRefresh, 2000), []); an effect calls retry() and setRefresh(false) when refresh is true and loading is false; an effect on [lastSignal, throttledSetRefresh] calls throttledSetRefresh(true) when lastSignal?.action is set; an effect returns () => throttledSetRefresh.cancel().

5. Polling: an effect on [isSignalsAvailable, pollingIntervalMs] returns early when isSignalsAvailable is true; otherwise it starts setInterval(() => setRefresh(true), pollingIntervalMs) and returns a cleanup that calls clearInterval.

6. Mark as read: an onMarkAsRead(id) callback calls notificationsApi.updateNotifications({ ids: [id], read: true }); on success it sets items to the previous items without that id; on rejection it calls toastApi.post({ title: t('unreadNotificationsCard.errors.markAsReadFailed'), status: 'danger' }) and leaves items unchanged.

7. Render in this order: if error, return <ResponseErrorPanel error={error} />; if items is undefined, return <Progress />; otherwise a Flex direction column gap 3 holding either <Text variant="body-medium" color="secondary"> with t('unreadNotificationsCard.emptyMessage') when items is empty, or one row per item, followed by a <Link to={root}> with t('unreadNotificationsCard.viewAll').

8. Each row is a Flex gap 3 align center with key notification.id: <NotificationIcon notification={notification} /> imported from '../NotificationsTable/NotificationIcon'; a Flex direction column gap 1 holding <Text variant="body-medium"> wrapping <Link to={`${root}?id=${encodeURIComponent(notification.id)}`}>{notification.payload.title}</Link> and <Text variant="body-small" color="secondary"> wrapping <RelativeTime value={notification.created} /> (imported as in NotificationsTable.tsx with the // @ts-ignore line); then <ButtonIcon aria-label={t('unreadNotificationsCard.markAsRead')} icon={<RiCheckboxCircleLine size={16} />} variant="secondary" onPress={() => onMarkAsRead(notification.id)} />.

9. Link, Progress and ResponseErrorPanel come from '@backstage/core-components'; Flex, Text and ButtonIcon from '@backstage/ui'; useApi and useRouteRef from '@backstage/core-plugin-api'; rootRouteRef from '../../routes'; notificationsApiRef from '../../api'.
10. UnreadNotificationsCardContent is a named function export with no release tag in its TSDoc (it is not part of the package entry).

units.behaviour: The notifications page reads ?id=, pins a deep-linked notification missing from the current page at the top, and highlights it.
rules: 1. const [searchParams] = useSearchParams(); const highlightedId = searchParams.get('id') ?? undefined; both placed after the existing useNotificationsApi call and before the first early return.
2. const pageNotifications = value?.[0]?.notifications; const missingFromPage = !!highlightedId && !!pageNotifications && !pageNotifications.some(n => n.id === highlightedId);

3. const { value: pinnedNotification } = useNotificationsApi<Notification | undefined>(api => missingFromPage && highlightedId ? api.getNotification(highlightedId).catch(() => undefined) : Promise.resolve(undefined), [highlightedId, missingFromPage]);
4. The notifications passed to the table are [pinnedNotification, ...(pageNotifications ?? [])] when missingFromPage and pinnedNotification are both set, otherwise pageNotifications.
5. NotificationsTable receives highlightedNotificationId={highlightedId}; filters, paging, title and totalCount stay as they are; without ?id the page behaves exactly as before.
